targets.authors: Bogaard, G., E. H. Meijer, A. Vrij, N. J. Broers, and H. Merckelbach.
targets.title: Contextual Bias in Verbal Credibility Assessment: Criteria-Based Content Analysis, Reality Monitoring and Scientific Content Analysis.
targets.evidence_quote: We therefore conducted a preregistered, direct replication of Bogaard et al. (2014; Experiment 2; CBCA condition), to verify the robustness of the contextual bias and better inform on the need for and way of de-biasing forensic credibility assessments.
targets.outcome_quote: Our results indicate a successful replication. Statements accompanied by positive (credibility-enhancing) information were rated as more credible and were given higher CBCA scores compared to those preceded by negative (credibility-reducing) information.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly state overall replication success for contextual effects on both CBCA scores and final credibility judgments.

reasoning: A completed preregistered direct replication with 105 newly recruited participants. The original-data recalculation in Section 5 informs design and power; the main paper is coded by its new-data replication. Subsequent contextual-bias studies are comparison/background, not additional targets.
